A year ago, I was visiting Argentina after my third year of college and got to chat with Vitor and Felipe over a video call. A few days later, I came to Brazil for the first time in my life to meet them in person. And a few days later, my two-week visit to Argentina turned into me moving to São Paulo and dropping out of Stanford to build Decade . If you know me, you know I've been obsessed with tech in LatAm forever. The way it can solve real-life everyday problems, improve our economies and give our talent somewhere to go. After an incredible wave of fintech innovations that gave everybody access to the financial system, the real-life everyday problems have now moved one level up: how to navigate that system. With economic volatility and an industry that is complex by design, managing your money is a second job for most people in Latin America. We're building Decade to solve that. While it was only Vitor and Felipe when I joined, one of my main motivations was the world-class team we were going to build. Today, I'm happy to say that my bet was right, and I get to work every day with the best early-stage team in the region, if not in the world. If you're serious about building the next LatAm tech giant, email careers@decade.com , or just DM me. This is only the beginning. Here's to the next Decade.

Feels like a 🥶 labor market! Yesterday the Fed held rates steady in a 9-3 vote. Three regional presidents wanted to hike. The majority wanted to hold. That's not consensus. That's a committee that genuinely doesn't agree on what the economy is doing. The June jobs report added 57,000 jobs, well below expectations. But unemployment ticked down. Wage growth moderated. Labor force participation dropped sharply. Each of those data points points in a different direction. The economy isn't sending a clean signal right now. What I do think is clear: this is a low-hire, low-fire market. Layoffs are not spiking. But hiring has slowed dramatically. Our data suggests that companies are cautious , and workers are staying put rather than taking risks on new roles. This kind of frozen market has its own risks in the long-term, including skills atrophy, which is especially concerning in the AI-age.
